content.thinking: This is a mid-rollout compatibility break: once a new writer starts emitting "2400/8" format while a still-old reader expects raw cents, that old reader throws a ValueError trying to parse it, exposing a real in-flight failure window.

hypotheses.summary: Revision 696c33a changed the summary cache entry from a bare cents integer to the text '{amount_cents}/{items_counted}'. The rollout is paused at 3 of 6 replicas. New-revision replicas write entries such as '2400/8', and the old-revision replicas still expect a figure in cents, so they fail reading them. Neither revision is faulty alone. The failure is the mix of two versions serving at once.

supporting_evidence.claim: Deployment of io-shop has not converged: 3 of 6 replicas are running revision [696c33a68b36aed6456cdc5b3806f33038488515], and 3 are still running revision [5470c1a64205bb28f9f2e8a96dc6ffa5eb2e611e]. Its rolling update is paused
ERROR io-shop: summary cache entry could not be read - ValueError: summary cache entry '2400/8' is not a figure in cents at src/io_shop/summary_cache.py (47 of 200 requests)
Diff: _ENTRY_FORMAT = "{amount_cents}/{items_counted}" added in summary_cache.py; the cache previously held a bare cents figure (summary_cents: int)
error_rate stepped from 0.005 to 0.055 then ~0.245 at 16:04-16:05 while p50/p95/p99 stayed flat

hypotheses.summary: Revision 696c33a is itself faulty: the new entry format breaks readers of the shared cache. The paused rollout makes this less likely than a version split.
